text:
Jana: Quick thought from the console review: for dashboards with mixed units we should surface a tiny conversion pill on hover: 'show in rps / show in reqs' so folks can flip units without leaving the chart. Screenshot: <link>
Tom: Nice. Also we need the legend to be denser for compact dashboards. Idea: replace full series name with truncated label + mini-histogram showing distribution. Helps spot spikes at a glance. Hover expands to full name.
Li: Mini-histograms are great but they must be keyboard-accessible. Make the hist a focus target and expose summary stats on focus. a11y: aria-describedby for the hist tooltip.
Riley: About axis labels: keep units short and consistent. Prefer `120 ms` over `0.12 s` when median < 1s. Use a rule: choose unit that keeps numbers >1 and <1000 if possible. Mention this in dev docs.
Jana: Agreed. Also add locale-aware separators and no unit duplicated in legend + axis. If the axis shows `ms` then legend shows just name + tiny badge `ms`.
Tom: Outlier handling proposals (different from earlier thread): 1) soft-compress scale using a sigmoid transform (preserves rank but compresses extremes), 2) gutter chevrons that expand the scale when clicked, 3) overlay a translucent "zoom to outliers" mini-view. Which one do we want default?
Li: My vote: gutter chevrons as default (explicit, discoverable), plus option to enable soft-compress per-chart. Soft-compress could confuse interpretations if people don't realize it's nonlinear. Add a subtle annotation when enabled: 'nonlinear scale applied'.
Riley: UX copy for the chevron: 'collapse extreme values' -> maybe too negative. Suggest: 'pin focus to range' / 'expand to include outliers' buttons. Keep wording action-oriented.
Jana: Good copy notes. For small multiples (sparklines grid) we should always show consistent Y scale option vs per-panel autoscale. Default should be consistent for dashboards comparing many series, but per-panel for detail views. Add a toggle in the toolbar: `Uniform Y` / `Independent Y` with tooltip.
Tom: Implementation note: for uniform Y we need to compute global percentiles without pulling full dataset per client. Backend should provide a baked range estimate endpoint. We'll show a loading skeleton for the legend hist until ready.
Li: Accessibility: make the sparkline focusable, expose a `role=button` with `aria-pressed` if it's selected for drill-in. Also ensure colorblind palettes for hist fills and spike markers. Provide a high-contrast border option.
Riley: Copy tweak in legend: replace `requests` with `requests · rps` and make the unit part muted. For missing units show a `—` and on hover include source: `derived from query: metric_type`.
Jana: Smoothing: default OFF for dashboards (we want raw signal), but show a non-blocking banner: 'Smoothing available: reduce jitter for trend reading'. The toggle opens a compact modal to pick window size and method (ema|rolling). The modal should have a quick preview.
Tom: Quick CSS snippet for keyboard reveal of the mini-hist:
```
.legend-entry:focus .mini-hist { transform: scaleY(1); opacity: 1; }
.mini-hist { transform: scaleY(0.9); opacity: 0.6; transition: all .12s ease; }
```
Li: Charts should expose a `data-units` attribute so assistive tech can announce units on focus: `aria-label="Latency, median 120 ms"`.
DesignBot: Note for release: add telemetry event `chart.unit_toggle` and `chart.outlier_mode_change` to track adoption. Default outlier_mode = "chevron".
Riley: One last nit: when we show mini-hists in legend, leave at most 4 bins horizontally so they remain legible in narrow sidebars.
Jana: I'll draft the copy and annotations for the prototype. Tom can wire up the storybook knobs. Pairing 11am tomorrow?
Tom: Yep, I'll build the story with toggles: Uniform/Independent Y, chevron/soft-compress, smoothing chooser.
Li: I'll send an a11y checklist and color token suggestions to the PR.
Riley: Thanks all. Leaving final microcopy to Jana. :sparkles:
